title: Show Them the Ceiling and the Floor of AI
author: Andrew Marcinek
summary: Marcinek argues that AI fluency means holding two truths at once: the technology is genuinely powerful and genuinely flawed. Students taught only to trust AI become marks; those taught only to fear it get left behind. He draws on research (a Harvard AI tutoring study, the BCG 'jagged frontier' study, lawyer sanctions for invented citations) to argue that classrooms need lessons that both showcase AI's power and deliberately expose its failures, so students develop real judgment rather than blind trust or blanket avoidance.
points: Teaching only AI's power creates 'marks'; teaching only its dangers creates students who get left behind — both are half-educations.
A Harvard-built AI tutor outperformed a well-designed active-learning physics classroom, suggesting AI can deliver the personalized tutoring Benjamin Bloom showed was so effective.
AI is 'annoyingly agreeable' (sycophancy) and confidently fabricates sources, as shown by lawyers sanctioned for filing briefs full of invented case citations.
The BCG consulting study found AI users did better on tasks the AI was suited for, but worse on tasks just outside its 'jagged frontier' — because the tool sounded equally confident either way.
Effective teaching pairs power lessons (using AI to genuinely accelerate learning) with poverty lessons (deliberately engineered failures) in the same unit.
quotes: I know it isn’t always right. I know it can be annoyingly agreeable — it will tell me my bad idea is a great one if I let it.
A Harvard team built an AI tutor for an introductory physics course and ran a controlled comparison against the university’s well-designed active-learning classroom
It invents sources that do not exist, complete with plausible authors and page numbers; lawyers have been sanctioned in federal court
The researchers called it the jagged frontier: AI’s abilities don’t fail gradually or predictably, they fall off a cliff mid-sentence
A student who has personally caught the machine inventing a citation is inoculated in a way no warning assembly will ever achieve.
